==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/wɪn/|a=RP,GA,CA,AU}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-win.ogg|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-win.wav|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|/wən/|a=NZ}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪn|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|win}} * {{hmp|en|wynn|winne|;|when> and <>>}} ===Etymology 1=== {{wikidata lexeme|L1245}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*wenh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|winnen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|winnan|t=to labour, swink, toil, }} (compare {{cog|ang|ġewinnan|t=conquer, obtain, gain; endure, bear, suffer; be ill}}), from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*winnan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*winnaną|t=to swink, labour, win, gain, fight}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wenh₁-|t=to strive, wish, desire, love}}. {{col-top|2|cog}} Cognate with {{cog|frr|wan}}, {{m|frr|wane}}, {{m|frr|wen}}, {{m|frr|wine}}, {{m|frr|wune|t=to win}}, {{cog|stq,fy|winne|t=to win}}, {{cog|cim|gabènnan|t=to win}}, {{cog|nl,nds|winnen|t=to win}}, {{cog|de|gewinnen|t=to win}}, {{cog|lb|gewannen|t=to win}}, {{cog|da|vinde|t=to win}}, {{cog|fo,is|vinna|t=to win}}, {{cog|nb|vinne|t=to win}}, {{cog|nn|vinna}}, {{m|nn|vinne|t=to win}}, {{cog|sv|vinna|t=to win}}, {{cog|got|𐍅𐌹𐌽𐌽𐌰𐌽|t=to suffer}}; also {{cog|la|venus|t=beauty, charm, elegance, grace; beloved, love}}, {{cog|sq|vuaj}}, {{m|sq|vuj|t=to suffer; to endure}}, {{cog|sa|वनोति|t=to desire, like, love, wish; to gain, procure; to win; to prepare; to hurt, injure}}. {{col-bottom}} ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ning|won,wan|won}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|transitive}} To [[conquer]], [[defeat]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1485|author=Sir Thomas Malory|title=Le Morte Darthur|section=Book IV |passage=For and we doo bataille we two wyl fyghte with one knyȝt at ones
and therfore yf ye wille fyghte {{long s}}oo we wille be redy at what houre ye wille a{{long s}}{{long s}}igne
And yf ye '''wynne''' vs in bataille the lady {{long s}}hal haue her landes ageyne
ye {{long s}}ay wel {{long s}}ayd {{long s}}ir Vwayne
therfor make yow redy {{long s}}o that ye be here to morne in the defence of the ladyes ryght}} # {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} To reach some destination or object, despite difficulty or toil (now usually intransitive, with preposition or locative adverb). #* {{quote-book|en|year=1908|author=Jack London|title=The Iron Heel|passage=No sooner did I get my freedom than my footsteps began to be dogged by the spies of the Iron Heel. It was necessary that they should be thrown off the track, and that I should '''win''' to California.}} #* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=VI|canto=I|stanza=23|passage=That euen in the Porch he him did '''win''',
And cleft his head a{{long s}}under to his chin}} #* {{RQ:Scott Marmion|passage=And when the stony path began,
By which the naked peak they '''won''',
Up flew the snowy ptarmigan.}} #* {{RQ:Stevenson Kidnapped|passage=“Has he nae friends?” said she, in a tearful voice.
“That has he so!” cried Alan, “if we could but '''win''' to them!—friends and rich friends, beds to lie in, food to eat, doctors to see to him—and here he must tramp in the dubs and sleep in the heather like a beggarman.”}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[triumph]] or achieve [[victory]] in (a game, a war, etc.). # {{lb|en|transitive}} To gain (a prize) by succeeding in competition or contest. #: {{ux|en|to '''win''' the jackpot in a lottery;  to '''win''' a bottle of wine in a raffle}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To obtain (someone) by [[wooing]]; to make an ally or friend of (frequently with ''over''). #* {{RQ:Sidney Arcadia|text=Thy virtue '''won''' me; with virtue preserve me.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare 6-1|V|3|text=She is a woman; therefore to be '''won'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1815|author=w:Jane Austen|title=w:Emma|volume=II|section=chapter 14| passage=Mr. Weston seems an excellent creature—quite a first-rate favourite with me already, I assure you. And she appears so truly good—there is something so motherly and kind-hearted about her, that it '''wins''' upon one directly.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To achieve victory. #: {{ux|en|Who would '''win''' in a fight between an octopus and a dolphin?}} #: {{ux|en|Nah, I'd '''win'''.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To have [[power]], [[coercion]] or control. #: {{ux|en|Ever since the 2013 Boston Marathon bombing, Bostonians now run as "One Boston." The terrorists did not '''win'''.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[obtain]] (something desired). #: {{ux|en|The company hopes to '''win''' an order from the government worth over 5 million dollars.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[cause]] a victory for someone. #: {{ux|en|The success of the economic policies should '''win''' Mr. Smith the next elections.}} #: {{ux|en|The policy success should '''win''' the elections for Mr. Smith.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|mining}} To [[extract]] (ore, coal, etc.).{{R:Raymond Glossary}} # {{lb|en|transitive|informal}} To [[defeat]] or [[surpass]] someone or something. # {{lb|en|computing|informal|intransitive}} To take priority. #: {{ux|en|If the local filters conflict with the global filters, the global filters always '''win'''.}} =====Conjugation===== ===Etymology 2=== {{wikidata lexeme|L15582}} From {{inh|en|enm|winn}}, {{m|enm|winne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|winn||toil, labor, trouble, hardship; profit, gain; conflict, strife, war}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*winną||labour, struggle, fight}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wenh₁-||to strive, desire, wish, love}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|Gewinn||profit, gain}}, {{cog|nl|gewin||profit, gain}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # An [[individual]] [[victory]]. #: {{antonyms|en|loss}} #: {{ux|en|Our first '''win''' of the season put us in high spirits.}} #* {{quote-journal |en |date=September 29, 2011 |author=Jon Smith |title=Tottenham 3 - 1 Shamrock Rovers |work=BBC Sport |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/15014632.stm |page= |passage=Giovani dos Santos smashed home a third five minutes later to wrap up the '''win'''.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120105133810/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/15014632.stm|archivedate=5 January 2012}} # {{lb|en|slang}} A [[feat]] carried out [[success]]fully; a [[victorious]] [[achievement]]. #: {{antonyms|en|fail}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[gain|Gain]]; [[profit]]; [[income]]. # {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[wealth|Wealth]]; [[goods]] owned. =====Derived terms===== {{col3|en|for the win|you win|win-win|no-win|stakeswin|winless|winrate}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|individual victory}} * Armenian: * Azerbaijani: * Bengali: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Danish: * Dutch: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Ingrian: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Korean: * Kurdish: * Macedonian: * Marathi: * Nepali: * Norwegian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Romansh: * Russian: {{t+|ru|вы́игрыш|m}}, {{t+|ru|побе́да|f}} * Sardinian: * Scottish Gaelic: * Swedish: * Tamil: * Telugu: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|feat, achievement}} * Bulgarian: * Danish: * Hebrew: * Italian: * Swedish: * Tamil: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|gain, profit}} * Azerbaijani: * Bulgarian: * Danish: * Finnish: * Galician: * Hebrew: * Italian: * Middle English: * Portuguese: * Swedish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|wealth, goods}} * Middle English: {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 3=== From {{inh|en|enm|wynne}}, {{m|enm|winne}}, {{m|enm|wunne}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wynn||joy, rapture, pleasure, delight, gladness}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wunnju}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wunjō||joy, delight, pleasure, lust}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*wenh₁-||to strive, wish, desire, love}}. Cognate with {{cog|de|Wonne||bliss, joy, delight}}, archaic {{cog|nl|wonne||joy}}, {{cog|da|ynde||grace}}, {{cog|is|yndi||delight}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|?}} # {{lb|en|Scotland}} [[pleasure|Pleasure]]; [[joy]]; [[delight]]. # {{alternative form of|en|wynn}}. =====Derived terms===== *{{col|en|worldly win}} ===Etymology 4=== From {{m|en|wind}}. ====Verb==== {{head|en|verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive|Scotland}} To [[dry]] by [[exposure]] to the [[wind]]. ===References=== {{reflist}} {{cln|en|strong verbs|irregular verbs|3-letter words}}
